facts.text: Elgin was founded by the Gifford brothers in 1835, named after a Scottish hymn, and incorporated in 1854.
Elgin High School counts five Navy admirals, a Nobel laureate, a Pulitzer winner, a Tony winner, two Oscar‑winning producers, Olympic athletes and a GM CEO among its alumni.
The Elgin watch factory, started in 1867, became the largest producer of fine watches in the U.S. and the world until it closed in 1965.
Historic Elgin’s Victorian architecture includes Queen Anne homes, and the city hosts the Hemmens Cultural Center and the Visual & Performing Arts Center for performances.
The Chicago Aurora and Elgin Railroad once linked the city to Chicago, making Elgin a key stop on the early commuter line.
